column2: “Sorry, but please ask someone else.”
At my words, Toshio snorted.
“...So you don't trust me.
Fine.{r}{p}Then Mr. Mikimoto,
could you go with them?{r}{p}You seem trustworthy.”
“But Mr. Mikimoto, you're injured!”
Mr. Mikimoto stopped {n2}'s protest with a wave of his hand.
“It's all right,
I can manage going upstairs.{r}{p}I did come down from there, after all.”
He said that with a feeble smile.
“Don't do anything that gets in the way of the police investigation.”
Mr. Kobayashi warned.
Of course, I'd like that too if possible.
But since I didn't even know what to look for, I couldn't promise anything.
I nodded for the time being, and the three of us went up to the second floor.
Standing before Mr. Tanaka's door, my feet felt chilled.
Cold air was seeping out from under the door.
“What exactly do you plan to investigate?”
Mr. Mikimoto asked.
I couldn't answer and silently opened the door.
Countless snowflakes were dancing around the room.
It was like a freezer.
Snow blowing in through the glassless window had by now covered more than half of the bed by the window.
“It's freezing!{r}{p}
I can't last five minutes in this outfit!”
{n2} cried, shivering.
I made up my mind and stepped inside,
and first opened the bathroom door.
As I was about to look inside, I heard a sound behind me like someone falling.
When I turned, {n2} and Mr. Mikimoto hadn't come in.
Is something wrong?”
No answer.
I had a bad feeling.
What if Mr. Mikimoto was the culprit?
Seizing a chance to get {n2}...
No, that couldn't be.
Even if he were the culprit, he'd have no need to harm {n2}.
“Mr. Mikimoto?”
The instant I stuck my head out the door to look into the hallway, a powerful shock shot from my skull down to my waist.
A blinding white light burst in my head, as if a strobe had been fired right in front of my eyes.
I was lying on the floor.
My vision spun and I couldn't stand up.
Unusually warm sweat ran down my temple and dripped onto the floor.
It wasn't sweat.
It was my blood.
The back of my head throbbed hot, as if some other creature were squirming there.
There were feet in front of me.
I summoned all my willpower and tried to lift my head.
With the ceiling light behind it and my eyes blurred, I couldn't tell who the pitch-black figure was
My eyes were fading...
The last thing I glimpsed was the figure slowly raising something.
They meant to kill me.
No.
I don't want to die.
I wanted to say stop, but no voice came out.
The figure swung something down, and the whistle of it cutting the air reached my ears...
But if one person couldn't do it, several could...
A terrible thought crossed my mind.
What if the office ladies had killed everyone together?
This is bad!
{n2} was with those possible culprits right now!
I dashed through the dining room and flew up the stairs.
It must have taken ten seconds or so to reach the office ladies' room.
Open up!”
I shouted as I knocked.
I heard a faint argument inside, but the door was soon opened.
{n2} burst out and threw her arms around my neck.
“Thank goodness...
you're safe.”
That was my line.
what about Mrs. Kayama?”
I asked, avoiding the gazes of the girls staring at us.
“She didn't come, but...”
I see.
Then let's go back to our rooms.”
I pulled {n2} by the hand out of the room.
“But...
wouldn't it be safer to stay together?”
Ignoring her protest, I silently pulled her into my room.
“...Hey, what's going on?
Earlier you said everyone should stay together...”
I closed the door and put a finger to her lips to silence her.
“Things have changed since then.{r}{p}Listen,
listen carefully.{r}{p}It wasn't Toshio who killed everyone.”
“...It wasn't Toshio...
who did it?”
I nodded.
“Toshio...
Toshio was attacked too.{r}{p}He'd been beaten, and he was still breathing when I found him, but...”
I couldn't go on, and just shook my head.
“Who on earth...
who did it?”
“...Those three girls.{r}{p}There's no one else it could be.”
{n2} looked dazed for a moment, then started to laugh.
“Those...
those girls?{r}{p}You're saying they're murderers?”
“I know it's hard to believe, but what else could it be?{r}{p}Do you think Mrs. Kayama could have done all this by herself?”
“I don't think so, but...”
“Right?{r}{p}
Then it can only be those three.{r}{p}There's no one left.{r}{p}Everyone's dead.{r}{p}Everyone's been killed!”
I ended up yelling at {n2}.
{n2}'s face twisted ugly with an expression of fear and grief.
I can't believe it!{p}
...I don't want to believe it...”
“I don't want to believe it either.{r}{p}But we have to.{r}{p}Face reality.”
For a while {n2} buried her face in my chest and let out sobbing sounds, then spoke in a small voice.
is it...
really true that everyone's dead?{r}{p}Toshio, and Uncle and Aunt, and Mr. Kayama too?”
“You saw Mr. Kobayashi's and Mr. Kayama's bodies too, {n2}, didn't you?{r}{p}I put my ear to Toshio's chest too, but his heart had completely stopped.”
The instant I finished saying that, the lights in the room went out.
“Eek!”
{n2} screamed and clung to me with all her strength.
a power outage, m-maybe?”
I tried to act calm, but my voice cracked.
Before my eyes, pitch darkness as if painted over.
I couldn't see even {n2}'s face, though it had to be close enough that I could hear her breathing.
it'll probably get fixed soon.{r}{p}It's almost morning anyway.”
Suppressing my fear, I said something that could only serve as a comfort.
As time passed, the window slowly became visible, and I could make out the outline of the room and {n2}'s silhouette.
Without letting go of each other's hands, we somehow managed to reach the bed.
“Stay still.
If we stay still, we'll be all right.”
I kept saying it as if to convince myself.
Little by little, the panic subsided.
...Until the sound of a door opening and a scream reached us from the hallway.
It was definitely a woman's scream, but I couldn't tell whose.
And after the scream came a dull thud of something striking, and the sound of a person falling to the floor.
Surely not...
Surely not...!
{n2}'s whisper was trembling.
“...Mrs. Kayama!”
That's right.
I'd been so busy protecting myself and {n2} that I'd forgotten about Haruko.
If I rushed out now, I might still be able to save her.
Even so, my body seemed to have gone rigid and wouldn't move at all.
Were the three girls out in the hallway right now beating Haruko and finishing her off?
Grinning, enjoying the killing...
I didn't hear footsteps, but I heard a door open and close somewhere
Before long, silence returned to the building.
A silence as if every living thing on earth had been lost.
go check what's happening.”
{n2} said in a tearful voice.
“...Okay.”
I swallowed hard.
She might still be alive...
like Toshio.
Even so, I didn't think there was anything we could do, but turning a blind eye was far too cowardly.
I patted {n2}'s shoulder reassuringly and stood up, moved through the darkness, and groped for a mop to pick up.
In case they were waiting outside the door, holding their breath.
Creeping softly to the door, I pressed my ear to it and listened to the hallway.
I heard no faint breath, no rustle of clothing.
I put my hand carefully on the knob and turned it very slowly.
Keeping my body always on the room side so the door couldn't be pushed open,
I opened it slowly.
Stretching out only my neck to peer into the hallway...
I saw it.
A figure that looked like Haruko lay collapsed in the hallway.
It was dark and hard to make out, but she definitely wasn't moving at all.
I hurriedly shut the door, locked it, and turned back
to {n2}.
“It's no use!{p}
She's been killed too!”
{n2} began to cry, stifling her voice.
Forgetting even to tiptoe, I went to {n2} and put my arm around her shoulders.
Her shoulders shook with every sobbing cry.
I felt that if I could just stop that trembling she'd stop crying, so I put all my strength into my arms.
Why is this happening?{r}{p}Everyone...
everyone was such a good person...
why?”
How could I possibly know.
{n2}.{r}{p}Calm down.{r}{p}If we don't calm down, we'll be killed too.{r}{p}We'll be killed too!”
“You're saying those girls will kill us?{r}{p}I still can't believe it!{r}{p}There's something like an evil spirit here.{r}{p}Or else a crazed murderer.{r}{p}A human being,
an ordinary human being, couldn't possibly do such awful things!”
An evil spirit...
I didn't want to accept such a thing.
But it was just as hard to believe that those girls could carry out such terrible murders over and over.
{n2} started saying something outrageous.
“...We have to go help those girls.”
wait a minute!{r}{p}That's just walking into getting killed!{r}{p}You can't set one foot outside!”
I desperately caught {n2} as she stood up to leave.
“So you're telling me you'll just let those girls die, {n1}?”
“That's not it!{r}{p}
I'm saying what if they're the killers?!”
As I shouted back, I thought, huh?
'Those guys'...
I just said 'those guys.'
Not 'that guy,' but 'those guys.'
Of course.
It's not one person but several.
“...What is it?”
“Just before he died, Toshio said, 'That guy got me.'{r}{p}If all three girls had ganged up on him, he wouldn't have put it that way, right?”
{n2} seemed to weigh my words for a while, then abruptly jumped to her feet.
“That's right!{r}{p}
They're not the killers after all.{r}{p}We have to go help them quickly!”
“Hey, wait!{r}{p}
It's dangerous outside!{r}{p}There are three of them, so they're safe as long as they stay in.”
“You don't know that!{r}{p}
They're just girls, aren't they?{r}{p}Is it fine as long as only we survive?{r}{p}I can't stand watching people get killed anymore!{r}{p}
I can't just let them die!”
I felt the same way.
Besides, I thought I'd done everything I could up to now.
But {n2}, only {n2}, I didn't want to see her meet a fate like that, no matter what.
Even if all three of those girls were innocent, I didn't want to put {n2} in danger to save their lives.
“No!{r}{p}
Don't stop me!”
{n2} pushed me aside and tried to open the door.
“Okay!{r}{p}
I'll go.{r}{p}I'll go, so promise me you'll stay here with the door locked.{r}{p}No matter how late I am, you won't leave this room.”
{n2} seemed to agonize for a while, but in the end decided to go along with my suggestion.
“...Okay.
I promise.{r}{p}But come back quickly.{r}{p}And...”
“Hm?”
be careful.”
“Of course.”
I took the mop handle in hand again, quietly opened the door, and slipped out into the darkness of the hallway.
When I nodded at {n2}, the door closed, and I heard the lock button being pressed.
There were windows at the landing and elsewhere, but it was still darker than inside the room.
I crept toward the girls' room.
I was pathetic for being scared of mere girls, but my heart was pounding and my mouth was bone dry.
Stopping, I quietly put my ear to the door.
No sound came from inside.
Maybe, as {n2} said, they really had nothing to do with it?
But if so, that meant a crazed killer like Jason was prowling around here.
I couldn't tell which was more frightening.
After a little hesitation, I knocked.
“...Who is it?”
After a while, a faint whisper reached me.
“It's me...
“No!{r}{p}
Don't come near!”
Kanako's hysterical scream echoed in the darkness.
Hearing that trembling voice made me feel they really couldn't be killers.
“Don't be afraid.{r}{p}Just now in the hallway, Mrs. Kayama seems to have been attacked.{r}{p}Only you, me, and {n2} are left.{r}{p}If we don't all stand up to it together, we'll all be killed
.{r}{p}Let's band together.
We'll gather in one of the rooms.”
“No way!{r}{p}
Who'd be fooled by words like that?!”
She seemed to think I was the killer.
Naturally.
I had suspected them too.
I wondered if there was some way to clear her suspicions, but gave up right away.
“...Then please listen from where you are.{r}{p}Don't open the door for anyone, no matter what.{r}{p}{n2} and I will be in that room over there, so if you sense danger, shout at once
.{r}{p}Okay?{r}{p}
Right away...”
That was when a scream came.
...From behind me.
I turned, but saw nothing moving in the darkness.
that voice...
who was that?”
Kanako's voice came from behind the door, but I didn't answer and ran.
Nearly slamming into walls in the dark, I made my way back to the room.
I stopped and stared at the door, left slightly open.
Why was the door...?
I hesitated to go inside.
Answer me, {n2}.
But no sound came from inside the room.
I pushed the door open with the mop handle.
The room was faintly brighter than the hallway, but not enough to make out {n2}.
What...
what on earth had happened to {n2}?
She must have just found a mouse or a cockroach...
I tried to convince myself of that.
I shouted at the top of my lungs, but again there was no answer.
My legs were shaking so badly I could barely stand.
I advanced into the room step by step.
A black shape lying on the bed gradually came into dim view.
Is that...
Is that {n2}?
It can't be...
I staggered toward the bed and reached out to the shape that didn't so much as twitch.
By the time I sensed a presence behind me and turned around, it was too late.
Something swung down before my eyes, and a flash burst in my head.
As I slowly fell, the figure I saw last was, unbelievably...
It was {n2}.
I couldn't believe it.
I didn't want to believe it.
But I had no choice but to think so.
With heavy steps I climbed the stairs and reached the office ladies' room.
The door was open.
I felt as if I had somehow expected this sight.
Kanako lay on her back on one of the beds.
No blood flowed, but her neck was bent at an odd angle.
Aki seemed to be sitting propped against the wall, and the wall was splattered with red like a watermelon smashed against it.
And then Keiko...
She had plunged headfirst into the glass, as if trying to escape through the window.
Her back was soaked in blood and her clothes were slashed to shreds.
She seemed to have been stabbed repeatedly with a knife or something.
I felt nothing.
Then I turned on my heel and went back to my room.
I opened the door and looked in, but no one was there.
When I turned around, I saw {n2} coming out of her own room.
She seemed startled for a moment to see me too.
But right away a relieved smile came to her face, and she walked quickly toward me.
I couldn't help noticing she had her right hand behind her back.
“{n1}!{p}Thank goodness.
You're all right.”
She approached with an expression of genuine joy.
When she was a few steps away, she suddenly sped up and leaped at me.
Me...
Are you going to kill even me, {n2}?
I squeezed my eyes shut and swung the mop in my hand
down at {n2}
“Kyaaaaaa!”
There was a sickening impact,
and the sound of a body hitting the floor.
When I opened my eyes, {n2} was lying on the floor, covering her face.
Shocked by what I'd done, I dropped the mop.
...are you okay?”
I got on my knees and crawled toward her.{g}
Bright red blood was welling between the fingers covering her face.
“I'm the one who wants to ask!{r}{p}{n2}, why...
why would you become a murderer...”
As I started to say that, I noticed something lying beside {n2}.
A necklace with a cross on it.
She must have gone to her room to fetch this.
I had mistaken it for her hiding a knife or something.
She hadn't been attacking me.
She had only been trying to hug me.
And I...
forgive me...
I thought you'd killed everyone.{r}{p}...{n2}!{r}{p}
Hang in there!”
{n2} slowly lowered her hands from her face and looked up at me.
The smile I thought I saw at the very end was probably an illusion.
Her eyes rolled back, showing only white.
I killed {n2}...
I killed {n2}...!
This is a dream.
I must be having a nightmare.
When I wake up,
I'll be lying in bed,
and {n2} will be pounding on the door.
'Get up already or we'll be late for breakfast!'
she'll be yelling.
And I'll take {n2}'s ski lessons until I'm exhausted,
improve a little, and go home.
Before long winter break will end and college will start,
and {n2} and I will somehow become an official couple,
and a few years after graduating we might even get married...
Why are tears pouring out when I'm thinking about happy things?
This is...
just a dream, and {n2} and I will go on with our fun ski trip, so there's nothing to be sad about...
I noticed someone standing before me because a shadow fell.
I slowly raised my head, but all my tear-filled eyes could see was a blurry outline.
“...Who
...is it?”
There was no answer.
All I heard was the sound of something cutting the air,
and a shock ran from the crown of my head to my toes.
The world spun, and then darkness rushed in.
The dream is ending...
Now I can finally escape this nightmare.
...wake me up quickly...
quickly...
The culprit is Haruko...
But could she have carried out all the crimes by herself?
I didn't think so.
She was probably an accomplice of Mr. Kayama.
And at the end she pushed Mr. Kayama down the stairs and killed him.
Even someone as weak as her could manage that much.
I decided to hurry back to the second floor.
As I climbed the stairs to the first floor,
I heard a scream.
From upstairs!
I tightened my grip on the mop handle and raced up the stairs to the second floor.
Reaching the office ladies' room, I knocked lightly.
“Who is it...?”
A whispered reply came at once.
It was {n2}.
“It's me,
open up!{r}{p}Toshio,
Toshio's been killed by someone outside too...”
I heard a bit of arguing inside, but the door was soon opened.
{n2} burst out and threw her arms around my neck.
“Thank goodness...
you're safe.”
She seemed to have been worried.
“What about Mrs. Kayama...?”
I went in, shut the door, and asked {n2}.
“She didn't come?”
All three office ladies were there, accounted for.
Then that scream earlier...?
did anyone leave the room?”
nobody did.”
...Strange.
The only person not here was Haruko.
Haruko was supposed to be the killer.
So who on earth screamed?
Was it someone we didn't know about who was the killer and attacked Haruko?
I didn't know.
Back to square one.
Suddenly I noticed the three at the back of the room huddled together, glaring at me with hostility.
what's the matter?
Why the scary faces?”
“Don't play dumb!”
Aki shouted, her eyes blazing.
“We heard that scream just now, too.{r}{p}We won't be fooled anymore.”
wait a second.{r}{p}You can't mean
you think I killed Haruko?!{r}{p}Give me a break!”
“But there's no one left but you!{r}{p}Didn't you say Toshio and Mr. Kayama are dead?”
“...That's true, but...{p}{n2}!{r}{p}
Say something for me.”
Looking to {n2} for help, I saw a complicated expression.
you can't possibly think I...”
“No!{r}{p}
I don't think you're a murderer, {n1}.{r}{p}I don't...
but...
when we heard the scream, we were all here...”
The one thing I couldn't bear was {n2} suspecting me.
I told them my deduction.
“...Listen.

I think the culprits were the Kayamas.{r}{p}If the two were accomplices, all those murders weren't hard.{r}{p}And at the very end, Haruko pushed Mr. Kayama down the stairs.{r}{p}What do you think?{r}{p}
It all fits, doesn't it?”
“Then what was that scream?”
Aki asked back suspiciously.
“An act by Haruko, of course.{r}{p}She wants us to think she was attacked too, to lure somebody out.”
The girls exchanged looks as if weighing my words.
“And if it isn't?{r}{p}We'd be leaving Haruko to die, you know?”
{n2} said in a reproachful tone.
“That's...
but that can't be.{r}{p}There's no one else, right?{r}{p}It's obviously an act!”
'You actually suspect me, don't you...?'
I swallowed those words.
“Besides, if there were someone else who attacked Haruko, it'd be too late for her anyway.”
As soon as I said it, I thought, uh-oh.
{n2}'s expression had changed.
I never thought you were such a cold person, {n1}.{r}{p}Never mind.
I'll go look by myself.”
“Wait!{r}{p}
What are you saying?!{r}{p}I can't let you do something that dangerous!”
{n2} ignored my protest, shook off my hand, and tried to leave.
“Leave me alone!{r}{p}
It's my choice!”
She opened the door and dashed out, so I hurried after her.
{n2} stopped in front of the Kayamas' room and pounded on the door.
“Mrs. Kayama!{r}{p}
Mr. Kayama!{r}{p}
Are you all right?!”
Complaining wouldn't help now that it had come to this.
I stood next to {n2} and turned the knob.
But it seemed to be locked and wouldn't open.
“It's no use, {n2}.
It won't open.”
“Go get the key from downstairs!”
{n2} said with an anguished look.
I figured they were probably holding their breath in there, but I didn't say so.
“Okay.
You go back to the room, {n2}.”
She hesitated for a while, but in the end gave in and went back to the office ladies' room.
After watching her go in and the door close, I went down the stairs.
I searched for the key at the front desk, but couldn't tell which was the key to that room.
There was probably a master key of some kind, but Mr. Kobayashi had probably kept it himself.
As I was wondering whether to go to Mr. Kobayashi's room to look for the master key,{p}
all the lights went out.
The girls screamed.
Haruko's safety was now beside the point.
I wanted to get back to {n2} as fast as possible.
But with the sudden blackout, I lost my sense of direction and couldn't even take a step.
A terrible thought seized me.
What if this blackout itself had been arranged by the culprit?
What if someone had cut the breaker somewhere and was lying in wait to wipe out the rest of us...
In the darkness I felt as if someone was watching me intently, and I held my breath.
Unless he had an infrared scope, even the culprit shouldn't be able to see me...
Even as I soothed myself with reason, I couldn't suppress the rising terror.
If the culprit wasn't Haruko, the only explanation was a killer we didn't yet know about, one who appeared and vanished at will.
Someone like that might be able to find me at once even in this darkness…
I had to hurry,
get to a safe place as fast as possible.
My heartbeat grew so loud it seemed to echo through the whole building.
Even if he couldn't see me, he could tell where I was by the sound...
I even felt that way.
After a while, the outlines of the stairs and such began to faintly appear in the darkness.
I headed slowly to the second floor.
Since that last scream, not a sound had come from the second floor.
As if everything had died out.
I banished the unpleasant thought from my mind.
They were surely just holding their breath, trembling with fear.
No matter how fearsome a killer, he couldn't possibly kill four people in an instant.
Hearing the floor creak faintly, I stopped.
Someone was very close!
I felt like I could even sense that someone's breathing.
I stiffened like stone and held my breath.
Are you there?”
It was {n2}.
Her voice was tight with fear, but my tension drained away all at once.
Groping forward, I touched {n2}'s body.
Why did you come out?!{r}{p}
It's dangerous!”
In the darkness we felt for each other and held on tight.
“...But
...the power suddenly went out...
and I thought something might have happened to you, {n1}, and then I just...”
{n2} had risked danger to come check on me...
I had never found anyone so dear.
“Anyway, let's go back there.{r}{p}If we stay out here, there's no telling when we'll be attacked.”
We moved down the hallway, arms firmly linked.
I couldn't tell which door was which room, or even where in the hallway we were.
After mistaking doors several times, we finally reached the office ladies' room.
“Coming in.”
The door wasn't locked.
We slipped inside together, shut the door, and locked it.
In the pitch dark, we made our way to the beds and felt around for a place to sit.
Then I stepped on something soft, nearly fell, and leaned against {n2}.
“Get it together, {n1}.”
I couldn't answer.
What was that just now...
What was that...
The room lights came on.
We both let out pathetic shrieks at the same time, stumbled backward, and fell on our butts in front of the bathroom door.
The whole room was a sea of blood.
Kanako,
Keiko,
and Aki too...
all had their throats slit, blood gushing out in torrents.
“Noooo!”
{n2} buried her face in my shoulder, trembling and wailing.
I stared blankly at the sight, thinking.
What kind of...
what kind of person could do this to three people...
I had definitely heard a scream, once.
But in that single moment, could someone slit three throats without any of them calling for help?
Had he crept up under cover of darkness and slit their throats one by one without a sound?
Or...
Disbelieving, I stared at the back of {n2}'s trembling head.
{n2} could have done it.
{n2}, who had been in the same room.
It was also odd that she alone had survived.
I was grateful she'd worried about me, but with a killer around, would a woman really wander out alone?
If she were the culprit, she'd have nothing to fear, so it wouldn't be strange for her to come out without a care.
let's go...
to a different room.”
{n2} said in a tearful voice.
...Is this an act too?
I no longer knew what was what.
In the current situation she seemed like the only possible culprit, but what about the other incidents?
There must have been crimes {n2} couldn't have committed...
Even so, I had no room to recall and check each incident one by one.
When I noticed, {n2} was staring at my face.
{n1}... you can't think I'm the culprit...”
I stayed silent, but that was the same as saying yes.
“That's...
there's no way I could do that!{r}{p}Look!{r}{p}
How could I do something...
something this horrible...”
I couldn't stand it and yelled back.
“I want to believe it too!{r}{p}{n2}, I...
I really liked you...{p}it wasn't some casual thing...
I really liked you...
but...”
I no longer knew what I was even saying.
you can't believe me after all.{r}{p}...I see.”
{n2} muttered in a hollow voice and pulled away from me.
hey.
Where are you going?”
“You don't want to be with a murderer, right?{r}{p}I'm going back to my room.”
{n2} said in a tone colder than I'd ever heard.
A voice in my heart ordered me to stop {n2}, but I couldn't.
Away from this horrific pile of corpses...
and from {n2}...
I wanted to get away from everyone and be alone.
There was nobody and nothing in this world I could trust.
I couldn't even trust myself.
I left the room as if following after {n2} and went back to my own room.
Once inside I locked the door and collapsed onto the bed.
Just fall asleep now...
That's what I thought.
What did it matter what happened?
I was terribly tired.
In heart and in body.
Sleepy.
Unbearably sleepy.
Then I heard the most hideous, longest scream I had heard yet.
It must have lasted about ten seconds.
Then it vanished as if abruptly cut off.
Silence returned.
